beats.text: The tulip crash that ruined Holland is mostly a story.
beats.note: Historian Anne Goldgar found little evidence of widespread financial ruin.

beats.name: Charles Mackay
beats.role: Wrote that substantial merchants were reduced almost to beggary, drawing partly on satirical Dutch poems and pamphlets.

beats.text: Far fewer people took part than the legend says.
beats.note: Goldgar counted about 285 traders in Haarlem, 60 in Amsterdam and 25 in Enkhuizen, and says those are underestimates.

beats.context: What 1,100 guilders for a Switsers bulb equalled in a master carpenter's wages. Rich merchants could afford it.

beats.text: She found virtually no bankruptcies traced to tulips.
beats.note: Bankruptcy records are patchy, so this is a lack of evidence, not proof.

beats.text: The real damage was to trust, in a society that ran on credit.
